title: test_embed fails if Python is built with LTO and LLVM clang on macOS
body: I am building CPython on macOS 10.12.6 with LLVM clang and LTO. During the PGO profile task, test_embed fails with 41 failures, while several other tests report environment changes. The source checkout initially identified itself as v3.12.0b1-1940-g77e9aae3837. Building Python 3.12.0 on the same system with the same toolchain only reports test_embed as having changed the environment, rather than producing the 41 failures seen on main.

symptoms_visible: During the PGO profile task on my macOS LTO build, test_embed fails with 41 failures and the build stops at profile-run-stamp.
Python 3.12.0 built with the same toolchain reports only that test_embed changed the environment.
N0.label: N0 LTO test_embed failure reported

symptoms_visible: Running test_embed directly produces many ImportError failures while loading extension modules, including missing _PyExc_ValueError and _PyBaseObject_Type symbols.
Running test_decimal by itself completes successfully despite the expected macOS allocation warnings.
N1.label: N1 failing extension imports isolated

symptoms_visible: I can import unicodedata normally from python.exe, but code run through Programs/_testembed cannot load extension modules.
Programs/_testembed test_init_main fails on 3.13 with an unresolved _PyBaseObject_Type symbol, while the same command works in 3.12.
The generated 3.13 Programs/_testembed contains no symbols.
N2.label: N2 failure isolated to embedded executable

symptoms_visible: The failure reproduces in a full-LTO build without PGO.
After reverting commit 3e3a7da590e1c3e5f03802e538f26c5204889c82 and rebuilding from scratch, the full test_embed suite passes.
N3.label: N3 regression and candidate backout measured

symptoms_visible: The same full-LTO failure occurs when I build with LLVM 16, and test_embed passes after backing out the same commit.
On another affected macOS machine using Apple clang, backing out the same commit also makes the build succeed.
N4.label: N4 macOS compiler variants confirm backout

symptoms_visible: I can successfully build Python 3.13.0a1 and current main with both PGO and LTO, and test_embed no longer fails.
N_terminal.label: terminal PGO and LTO builds succeed

question_patterns: Exactly how did you configure and build Python?
Can you share the configure command, including optimization and LTO options?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I configured it with `CC=clang CXX=clang++ CPPFLAGS=-I/usr/local/include LDFLAGS=-L/usr/local/lib ./configure --enable-optimizations --with-lto=full`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I used the default Apple compiler and a plain `./configure` build without either LTO or PGO.
The include and library paths differ, but the build still uses clang, `--enable-optimizations`, and `--with-lto=full`.

question_patterns: Does test_decimal fail when you run it by itself?
Can you run `python.exe Lib/test/test_decimal.py` and report the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran `python.exe Lib/test/test_decimal.py`. It prints the documented macOS allocation warnings, but the tests complete successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone decimal test still passes, but it prints a different number of the documented allocation warnings.

edges.comment: The reporter also volunteered the direct test_embed output, which isolates real failures to unresolved symbols in dynamically loaded extension modules rather than the expected test_decimal warnings.

question_patterns: Can you import unicodedata manually with the built python.exe?
Was unicodedata built, and does importing it from the normal interpreter work?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. In `python.exe`, my sys.path includes the source Lib directory and the build extension directory, and `import unicodedata` succeeds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, `import unicodedata` fails the same way in the normal python.exe process.

edges.comment: The normal interpreter can load the module. The reporter then compared Programs/_testembed across 3.12 and 3.13 and inspected the generated executable, finding the failure only in the 3.13 embedding executable.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this without PGO, using only `--with-lto=full`?
Does a clang full-LTO build still fail test_embed when optimizations and the PGO profile task are omitted?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I was testing with full LTO and without PGO, and the embedding tests still fail. Everything works when I build Python without LTO.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. An LTO-only build passes; the failure occurs only during the PGO profile task.

question_patterns: Can you bisect the test_embed regression using a profile task limited to test_embed?
Which revision does your bisection identify between the working and failing builds?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection identifies an unrelated runtime module-loading change, and reverting 3e3a7da590e1 has no effect.
The same commit is identified when I use a narrower good/bad range.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild from scratch after reverting that revision and rerun test_embed?
Please test a local build with the candidate commit backed out and report the raw test result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After reverting `3e3a7da590e1c3e5f03802e538f26c5204889c82` and rebuilding from scratch, `./python.exe -m test -v test_embed` passes all of the applicable tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean rebuild with that commit reverted still produces the same unresolved-symbol failures.

edges.comment: These are handler-initiated isolation, bisection, and candidate-backout measurements. The reporter supplies the raw commit hash and pass/fail output; interpreting that commit as the NoLTO regression is engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you repeat the macOS build with LLVM 16 and test both the original revision and the candidate backout?
Does this reproduce with LLVM 16 rather than LLVM 17?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The issue also exists when I build with LLVM 16, and backing out commit 3e3a7da resolves it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: LLVM 16 builds test_embed successfully without backing out anything; only LLVM 17 fails.

question_patterns: Can another affected macOS system share its compiler and confirm whether the same backout changes the result?
Does the same backout resolve the benchmarking machine's failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm also seeing it on macOS 13.6 arm64 with Apple clang 14.0.3, using `--enable-optimizations --with-lto`; backing out 3e3a7da resolves it for me too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same backout works on a different macOS release and Apple clang patch version.

edges.comment: The second affected macOS reporter is folded into the simulated user side. The reproductions show that the regression is not specific to LLVM 17 or the original macOS 10.12 machine.

solution.intent: Revert the NoLTO linking change introduced by commit 3e3a7da so macOS clang full-LTO builds no longer produce a symbol-less Programs/_testembed, then ask the reporter to verify a current build containing the revert.
solution.concrete_example: Revert commit 3e3a7da590e1 through PR #110720. The failing build was linking objects carrying LTO information into Programs/_testembed under the NoLTO path on macOS, producing an executable with no usable exported symbols; extension modules loaded by embedded Python then could not resolve symbols such as PyBaseObject_Type. Please rebuild today's main with your normal PGO+LTO configuration and rerun test_embed before considering this resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The bisection output only identifies commit 3e3a7da590e1. Mapping that revision to the NoLTO optimization and concluding that mixing LTO objects with the non-LTO testembed link path caused the malformed, symbol-less executable is the technical inference. The thread treats the exact LLVM linker mechanism as not fully understood, but the commit-level cause and backout are confirmed on multiple macOS clang configurations.

edges.comment: PR #110720 reverted the NoLTO change. The reporter later verified Python 3.13.0a1 and current main with both PGO and LTO; closure and compiler-version updates are not independently scored logistics.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the regression as commit 3e3a7da590e1's NoLTO linking change, which caused macOS clang full-LTO builds to produce an unusable Programs/_testembed with no symbols.

Must connect the malformed Programs/_testembed to the observed runtime import failures: embedded Python could not resolve CPython symbols such as PyBaseObject_Type and PyExc_ValueError when loading extension modules.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the full-LTO-only reproduction, the bisection output, the clean local backout test, and confirmation on additional macOS clang configurations.
The corrective action must revert the NoLTO change rather than treating test_decimal allocation warnings, file-descriptor limits, or general memory pressure as the cause.
Must ask the reporter to rebuild and verify test_embed on a current build containing the revert before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical CPython source builder comfortable with clang toolchains, LTO and PGO configuration, git bisection, symbol-table inspection, clean rebuilds, and direct execution of embedding test programs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Evidence-driven and precise; posts exact commands and raw output, corrects platform-specific symbol-name misunderstandings, distinguishes observations from guesses, and follows up with cross-version and cross-compiler tests.
